So you're riding your bike in jeans or some nice khaki pants, but your pants leg keeps hitting the chain wheel. Not only can this potentially cause your pants leg to get caught in the chain, but it will leave streaks on them. What to do? You can try a chain wheel guard. You can also go for a full chain guard. This is just adding weight to your bike, and you're still going to be partially distracted by your pants leg hitting that. You can roll up your pants leg, but then you look like a hipster, plus your pants could just unroll on their own while you're riding, and you don't want that.

You can also strap your pants leg. My local bike shop had little reflective velcro leg bands for 3 dollars each. I was lucky. Buying them online can cost a lot more. You can also just make your own.

Lots of stores with craft sections will sell velcro strips for dirt cheap. You can simply cut these to make your own leg straps. If they sell velcro strips that have the sticker glue on one side for sticking them to flat surfaces, you can simply glue two opposing velcro strips back-to-back and you're basically done. That's about as easy as it gets.

You can also make them from a strip of duct tape folded over itself. Add some stickable velcro pads to the ends. Any crafts section will have velcro stickers.

Duct tape comes in lots of different colors besides just grey. I prefer black duct tape. I also have some dark blue duct tape that would probably match a pair of jeans pretty well.

If you make it from duct tape, you can also add reflective tape to it. Any auto parts store will have reflective tape. Walmart also sells rolls of white or red reflective tape.

Another option if you're good with crafts is to buy the kind of button snaps for clothing, take a strip of fabric that matches your pants and is just long enough to go around your ankle with a little room so you're not strangling it, and add the button snaps to both ends. Now you've got a little piece of fabric that can blend in with your pants.

Lastly, you can simply put a rubber band around your ankle. That might be too tight, but it's simple and it should work.

There you go! You've now solved an age old problem without modifying your bike, and you did it for cheap.
